title: Double guns: ultra-class haul truck packs dual-gun MCS charging, 4 MWh battery
summary:
NHL may not be a household name, but its all-new, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.

title: GM’s V2G pilot wants to pay California drivers for power from parked EVs
summary:
GM Energy and WeaveGrid are launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) pilot that will let select Southern California Edison (SCE) customers send electricity from their EV batteries back to the grid. Eligible drivers could get more than $16,000 in help with equipment and installation, and earn money when the grid needs their power.

title: NSSL keeps growing its electric terminal truck fleet, with no plans to stop
summary:
After taking delivery of its first Orange EV e-Triever electric yard tractor in 2024, NSSL saw the electric light. The company has been moving quickly to transition its yard tractor fleet to zero emissions, and its efforts haven’t gone unnoticed: NSSL is now being recognized by the 2026 Canadian Clean Fleet Awards.

title: Alpitronic’s new SC plant to build 400 kW and 1 MW fast chargers
summary:
Alpitronic, the company behind IONNA’s fast chargers, is investing nearly $34 million in a new South Carolina factory. It’ll build 400 kW DC fast chargers, plus a 1 megawatt (MW) system that can charge cars and heavy-duty trucks.

summary:
Who doesn’t love a good fastback? BYD’s new Han was spotted completely undisguised, giving us an early look at its sleek design and interior ahead of its expected debut next week.

title: Kia’s cheapest EV is coming next year, and it could cost under $25,000
summary:
Kia’s EV lineup covers just about every size and price point, but it believes one thing is still missing: a truly cheap electric car. That’s about to change in 2027, when Kia plans to unveil a new EV that could start at around $22,000 to $24,000.

title: Hyundai claims 2027’s ‘Best EV Brand’ title as the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 impress
summary:
Hyundai’s electric SUVs are getting some love. The IONIQ 5 and three-row IONIQ 9 helped the Korean automaker land its first-ever “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” award from US News & World Report for 2027.

title: BYD’s folding steering wheel isn’t a concept — it’s in a $49K SUV now
summary:
BYD launched a production SUV today with a steering wheel that folds flat into the dashboard. It comes standard on the top trim of the Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9, which sells for 329,900 yuan (about $49,000) in China.

Automakers and suppliers have been parading folding wheels on concept cars for about a decade. This is the first one customers can actually order, according to BYD.

title: The Volkswagen ID. Buzz Beach is an electric van built for camping, but it’s not cheap
summary:
Volkswagen introduced the ID. Buzz Beach, a fun spin on its electric van that’s built for camping and overnight stays. However, it won’t be cheap, starting at over $70,000.

title: Aptera (SEV) completes its first customer solar EV — for its top crowdfunder
summary:
Aptera (SEV) has finished building its first solar electric vehicle for a paying customer. It’s going to Martin Hartono, the startup’s No. 1 “Accelerator” investor, and it’s being exported out of the US.

It’s a real milestone for a company that has pushed back its delivery dates since 2022. And it comes a week after Aptera reported $9.2 million in cash against the roughly $25 million it says it needs to start series production.

title: Elon Musk announces another Tesla vehicle no one asked for
summary:
Elon Musk says Tesla plans to build a version of the Model Y with no steering wheel and no pedals, a driverless people-mover he describes as “good for transporting groups of 6 or 7 people.”

It’s yet another vehicle nobody asked for, from a company that ended Model S and Model X production this year and is about to end the Cybertruck. And the data says very few car buyers want a car they can’t drive.

title: Porsche’s newest electric car is a tiny 50 mph replica of a legendary racer
summary:
Porsche’s latest electric vehicle isn’t a new Taycan or Macan EV. In fact, it’s not even a full-sized car. Instead, the German automaker has teamed up with British luxury miniature car builder Hedley Studios to create an 80%-scale electric replica of one of Porsche’s most iconic racing cars, the legendary 550 Spyder.

title: The world’s biggest oil shock could give EVs and solar a boost
summary:
The longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home. That’s one of the big takeaways from the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) new “World Energy Outlook 2026,” which examines how the biggest oil supply shock on record could speed up the shift to EVs and solar.

summary:

The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.

summary:
BYD is preparing to launch a new midsize SUV under its personalized, off-road-focused sub-brand. The new SUV was spotted testing, offering an early look at its boxy, rugged-looking design.

title: IONNA enables Plug & Charge for Tesla, opens 22 bay site in Westminster, CA
summary:
IONNA, the DC charging operator backed by several major OEMs, has opened its largest DC charging site yet, with 22 bays of 400kW charging in Westminster, California.

Alongside the opening, IONNA is also enabling Plug & Charge operation for Tesla EVs, with Stellantis EVs “coming soon.”

title: Kia went from this one quirky EV 40 years ago to an entire electric lineup
summary:
The Kia Besta EV hit the roads in 1986 as the brand’s first fully electric vehicle. 40 years later, Kia continues to “lead the pack” with a full lineup of EVs ranging from entry-level cars and SUVs to three-row models, and just about everything in between.

title: Tesla toughens FSD driver monitoring in Europe while loosening it in the US
summary:
Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).

In the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way. Its CEO told owners they can text and drive on FSD, and recent US builds were tuned to nag drivers less.

title: Rivian’s ALSO pauses high-tech e-bike deliveries over ‘software issues’ that we saw coming
summary:
Rivian’s new electric bike spinoff, ALSO, has hit another speed bump. The company has announced that it is temporarily halting deliveries of its TM-B electric bicycles after discovering software-related problems affecting some bikes, including issues with charging behavior.

more…

title: West Coast Customs turns a Tesla Model 3 into a 1955 Chevy Bel Air
summary:
West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint. The Burbank shop cut the body off a Tesla Model 3, kept the entire rolling platform, and set a 1955 Bel Air shell on top of it.

The result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door. And it charges at Tesla Superchargers.

title: Ford’s first LFP batteries are en route, and the $30,000 Fathom EV pickup will get them first
summary:
Ford has entered the battery business. The first LFP battery cells are now rolling off the assembly line at Ford’s BlueOval Battery Park plant in Michigan and are headed to power Fathom prototypes in Kentucky.

more…

title: Amflow launches its first city e-bikes, packing huge torque and serious smart tech
summary:
Amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the company is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment. The newly unveiled Amflow UE Carbon series marks the brand’s first move into the commuter e-bike market, combining a lightweight carbon fiber frame, powerful mid-drive motor, and a surprisingly long list of smart features designed for everyday riding.

And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.

more…

title: Tesla’s Semi Megacharger network hits 7 sites, far short of 37 goal
summary:
Tesla has opened its first Semi Megacharger in Texas, an 8-stall station in Mesquite on the east side of Dallas. With it, Tesla’s map now lists 7 public Megacharger sites and 44 stalls for its electric truck.

That’s progress. But with six weeks left in 2026, it’s less than a fifth of the 37 sites Tesla planned to have open this year.

title: Volvo EWR150 Electric wheeled excavator gets to work in Luxembourg
summary:
As no-drip, low-noise job sites become more the global rule rather than the exception, Volvo’s incredibly versatile EWR150 Electric wheeled excavators are proving to be a smart addition to construction and municipal fleets – that’s proving true in Luxembourg, as well.
